title: Presence, colour mixer and vignette modules
objective: Deliver Texture, Clarity and Dehaze as a Presence module, a Lightroom-style HSL colour mixer module and a post-crop Vignette module over the delivered editor: the host stage and ordering additions, the tiled spatial primitive and positional colour units they need, frozen numerical contracts for each, generated controls and API methods with verified UI/API parity, exact fixtures, native M4 rendered evidence and recorded photo-sized measurements, per the proposed design.
context_summary: Basic is one pointwise colour layer with field patches, the core draft lifecycle and streamed colour runs; the UI components vocabulary already has sliders with gradient rails, groups with resets and collapsed sections, so no new control kind is expected. The host places layers by stage only, which cannot order the mixer after Basic, keep local contrast after the pointwise run, or put a vignette after the crop. The design adds spatial and finish stages, an order within a stage, a tiled halo-bounded spatial primitive with a bounded sample path and cached global estimates, and position-aware colour units. Each module's equations are frozen by a numerical study against independent f64 references before its module task starts. Provisional performance targets are the Basic ones; a measured miss is reported, not hidden.

tasks.description: Add the spatial and finish effect stages, the per-effect order within a stage, the new placement rules (pixel and colour before the first spatial or geometry layer; spatial before the first geometry layer; geometry before the first finish layer; finish at the end; order-aware insertion within a stage), position-aware PointwiseColor rows, and compile-time refusal of a finish layer followed by a geometry layer, with no module yet using them.
extra_context: Existing layers never move; every delivered module keeps its stage, order 0 and its current stack positions, so the M1 to M4, Basic and RAW fixtures must still evaluate byte-identically.

apply_row gains the row's y and starting x; every delivered unit ignores them. The RAW linear path passes the same coordinates for its terminal per-pixel evaluation so sample_linear and render_linear stay in agreement.
Performance checklist: registration and placement stay descriptor-only hash work; no new allocation, frame work, owner-thread image work or timer.

Evidence: EffectStage spatial and finish, EffectDescriptor.order (serialized, default 0), insertion_index(layers, stage, order) with the full placement table and insertion_index_for(effect), apply_row(y, x0, rgb) on the byte and linear paths, and the finish-before-geometry compile refusal are implemented with placement tests over every stage and both orders, the refused-order tests through the registry and EditorService, positional render/sample parity tests on both paths, and module.list round trips; the module design's tables list them. Workspace suites pass unchanged (core 254 unit tests plus integration suites, app 188). check-repository passes. No allocation, owner frame work or timer added; apply_row is called once per row inside the existing chunk scratch.

tasks.description: Numerical study for Presence: select and freeze the texture band, the clarity base and compressive curve, and the dehaze atmospheric model (global estimate, transmission, floor and negative strength) against independent f64 references, fixing each unit's scales, halos at 24 MP and 60 MP, tiled-versus-whole-frame tolerance, halo bound on edge fixtures and production tolerance, and record them in a presence study note.
extra_context: Candidates come from the darktable and Lightroom research: guided-filter and downsampled-base decompositions are preferred because they tile; a local-Laplacian candidate is rejected unless it tiles within the 512 pixel summed halo.

Fixtures: step edges, sinusoidal frequency sweeps, textured patches, smooth 8-bit gradients (to record the extra quantization boundary's effect), noise at several amplitudes, and a synthetic hazed image built from the forward model with known transmission and atmospheric light so recovery is measurable.

The note follows the tone study's form: equations, monotonicity or boundedness proofs where claimed, limitations, the frozen tolerance and the fixture files. It documents current behaviour to build, not history.

Evidence: docs/design/presence-study.md freezes dehaze then texture then clarity: finite-support box, min and box-guided filters evaluated in a fixed order, Clarity and Dehaze on a 4x reduced base anchored at the frame origin, radii quoted at a 6000 px long side and scaled with a cap at 10000, a tanh compressive gain in the encoded domain that never creates clipping, dark-channel dehaze with a guided transmission, a 0.1 floor and an atmospheric light from the 1/16 reduction (24 bytes), a uniform veil for negative amounts, summed halos 46/274/448 px at 480/6000/10000 (bound 512), and a 2e-4 + 2e-4|ref| production tolerance derived from measured f32 filter error through the dehaze path; tests/reference/presence.rs, tests/presence_reference.rs (43 tests, including bit-identical tiled evaluation at three tile sizes) and fixtures/presence/ (10 oracle cases, 76 measurements) are checked in. The note records that a single 512 px tile needs about 57 MiB of scratch at 60 MP, which the design answers with a separate 256 MiB spatial budget and batch-limited concurrency.

tasks.description: Numerical study for the colour mixer: freeze the eight Oklab hue-range basis functions (centres, overlap, partition of unity, chroma ramp), the hue rotation, chroma scaling and luminance response for the −100..+100 ranges, the gamut policy and the production tolerance against an independent f64 reference, and record them in a mixer study note.
extra_context: Reuse the colour study's Oklab conversion, achromatic-axis rule and near-black handling. Required properties: every slider at 0 is the exact identity; achromatic pixels are invariant under every slider; a range's slider changes no pixel with zero weight for that range; hue is continuous around the wheel; luminance response is monotone.
Fixtures: the eight sRGB reference colours, an achromatic ramp, near-black chroma, a hue wheel at several chroma levels and portrait-like skin tones.

Evidence: docs/design/mixer-study.md freezes the Oklab basis (eight centre hues, raised-cosine partition of unity, chroma ramp C0 = 0.02), per-direction half-gap hue travel, saturation gain 1 with a non-negative factor, the gamma luminance response 2^(-m) with pass-through above white, hue then chroma then luminance from input weights, and the 1e-5 + 1e-5|ref| tolerance; tests/reference/mixer.rs, tests/mixer_reference.rs (43 tests) and fixtures/mixer/mixer-cases.json (414 cases) are checked in; measured figures (exact partition of unity, identity residual 3.9e-7, grey deviation 2.6e-7, minimum single-slider hue slope 1 - pi/4, the one documented opposing-slider fold) are recorded in the note.

tasks.description: Numerical study for the vignette: freeze the mask (midpoint, roundness and feather geometry over the output stage), the negative and positive amount equations in linear light, symmetry and centre-invariance properties and the production tolerance against an independent f64 reference, and record them in a vignette study note.
extra_context: Required properties: amount 0 is the exact identity for every mask; the centre pixel is unchanged for every parameter combination; the mask is symmetric under mirror and flip and depends only on the stage size and parameters; negative amount at −100 reaches black at the corners; positive amount never exceeds the display white in encoded terms.
Fixtures: flat fields and gradients at several aspect ratios with parameters at their extremes and defaults; corner and centre samples hand-computed.

Evidence: docs/design/vignette-study.md freezes pixel-centre coordinates, the roundness shape radius (quadratic blend for s >= 0, p-norm with p = 2 + 6(-s) for s < 0), the smoothstep falloff between r0 = m(1 - f) and r1 = m + (1 - m)f with a hard step at zero width, the linear darken and encoded lighten amount branches, the 1e-6 + 1e-6|ref| tolerance, and the corner-saturation condition (corner mask = 1 iff r1 <= r_corner) that replaces the design's unconditional corner claim; tests/reference/vignette.rs, tests/vignette_reference.rs (41 tests) and fixtures/vignette/ (202 mask and 60 amount cases) are checked in.

tasks.description: Implement the spatial primitive in the host: Processing::Spatial with at most four SpatialUnit units, the stage boundary in compile and segment evaluation on the JPEG and RAW paths, tiled 512 × 512 halo-bounded execution on the shared Rayon pool with a separate 256 MiB spatial budget and batch-limited concurrency, cancellation between tiles, compile-time refusal of an over-bound halo or an over-budget tile, the 1/16-scale global-estimate reduction with its eight-entry cache, and the bounded point-sample path through a spatial layer.
extra_context: Proved with a test unit (a box blur with a declared halo and a global mean estimate), not with the presence units: tiled output agrees with a whole-frame reference within the frozen tolerance for tile sizes 128 and 512 and is deterministic across runs; render.sample through the unit equals the rendered byte because it evaluates the stage-aligned tile that contains the point; a sample allocates at most one tile and, on an estimate cache miss, one 1/16-scale reduction. On the RAW linear path the operation pulls its input tiles through the compiled prefix and writes one float frame the rest of the evaluation pulls from.

At most two full frames exist at once; the frame limit, scratch budget and one-megapixel threshold are unchanged. No full-frame float buffer on the JPEG path. Nothing runs on the owner thread. Neutral operations compile to nothing and keep source sharing.

Performance checklist: new allocations are the tile planes (bounded by the scratch budget), the reduction (at most 0.25 MP) and the estimate store (at most 32 KiB); measured 24 MP and 60 MP before/after render figures recorded with scope.

tasks.description: Implement the vignette module: descriptor (finish effect, Amount, Midpoint, Roundness and Feather number parameters with defaults, one group with sliders and a module reset, collapsed section after Crop), the set-vignette field patch and reset-vignette, labels and values, and the frozen positional unit compiled against the output stage.
extra_context: Production matches the vignette study's f64 reference within tolerance on the JPEG and RAW paths; the centre is byte-invariant; the mask is symmetric under the transform module's mirror and flip; updating the crop layer in place recentres the vignette and updating the vignette never moves the crop.
A stored stack with the vignette before a geometry layer is refused by the host rule from the stage task; this module adds no second rule.
Performance checklist: one positional pointwise unit, the mask evaluated per row from the stage size, no allocation beyond row scratch, latency recorded.

Evidence: lightwell.vignette (collapsed, finish stage, effect lightwell.vignette.postcrop because identity segments forbid hyphens, single layer) with amount, midpoint, roundness and feather defaults filled for missing keys, amount 0 neutral, set-vignette patch and reset-vignette, labels and values, one positional unit with f64 per-row and per-column mask tables and the production extended encode/decode for the positive branch; production matches the 202 mask cases to 1.1e-16 and the 60 amount cases within the frozen 1e-6 tolerance, and both fixture files within one output code through the real render path; the layer stays last through rotate, mirror and crop edits, recentres after a crop update, is mirror and flip symmetric byte for byte, keeps the shared source when neutral, and render/sample agree on both paths after a crop resample. Measured single-threaded apply_row over 6000x4000 in release on the M4 Pro: 57 ms at amount -50, 505 ms at +50 (encode/decode per channel), 164 ms at roundness -100. Workspace suites, clippy and check-repository pass.
